subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing options for Atlas Therapeutics pilot
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@atlastx.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing question for pilot

Hi Grace / Karthik —

We're scoping a 6–9 month pilot for Atlas Therapeutics and need a quick sanity check on what you would recommend for dedicated capacity. High level: ~12 inference endpoints, most requests are short (<256 tokens) for classification and reranking, with occasional longer batch jobs (≤8k tokens) for nightly evaluation. Expected steady QPS per endpoint is ~3–5 qps, but peak windows could double that for hourly experiments.

Two questions:
1) Rough cluster size / minimum GPUs you'd expect for a safe starting point?
2) What reasonable ramp schedule and warmup (activation) plan do you typically propose for risk mitigation?

We need this to align to our budgeting conversation with procurement next week. Happy to share a simple traffic map — attached is our internal model (light read).

Thanks —
James
James Lee
Head of ML Platform
Atlas Therapeutics

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: James Lee <james.lee@atlastx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question for pilot

James —

Thanks for the traffic snapshot. I took a pass and sketched three pragmatic options that balance cost, availability, and operational safety. Attached: redwood-dedicated-options-ATX.pdf (summary) and a toy workbook (ATX-MAP-v1.xlsx) referencing your traffic numbers.

Option A — Conservative (fast fail-safe)- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs- Min guaranteed GPUs: 6- Ramp: 2x week 1 (warm), +2 GPUs week 3, evaluate at week 6; target steady at week 8- Notes: low cost relative to other options; relies on aggressive prefix caching and smaller batch windows. Good for short experiments you want to iterate on quickly.

Option B — Balanced (recommended for pilot)- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs- Min guaranteed GPUs: 10- Ramp: pre-warm 4 GPUs day 0, bring to 8 by week 1, 12 by week 3, steady 10–12 by week 6; built-in 48–72h burst allowance for experiments- Notes: supports the 3–5 qps per endpoint comfortably with room for planned hourly peaks; nightly 8k-token jobs use spare capacity with controlled QoS.

Option C — Resilience-first (production preview)- Cluster: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs- Min guaranteed GPUs: 20- Ramp: staged across 4 weeks with canaries, reserve burst window for heavy evaluation windows- Notes: best latency headroom and parallel batch throughput; more expensive but minimizes risk of throttling.

Warmup & activation approach (applies to all options):
- Day 0: pre-warm minimal pool (2–4 GPUs) and validate topology with synthetic load
- Week 1: run traffic shadowing (send copy of live prod traffic) and measure KV cache hit curves
- Week 2–4: progressive activation by endpoint group with canary rollback triggers (error rate, 95th latency)
- Ongoing: keep a small hot-standby pool for <1h bursts and a scheduled weekly health-check job

I'll loop Karthik for pricing cadence + credits. If you want, we can convert Option B to a 12-month commitment with a stepped discount — helps procurement.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T08:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question for pilot

James — quick follow-up with rough price points and a proposal structure. Grace's Option B aligns to most pilots we convert; below are ballpark numbers and commercial levers.

Option B (16 GPUs, min 10) — commercial snapshot- Monthly baseline commit (min 10 GPUs): $55,000/month- Elastic bursting (on top): $8,000 per 4-GPU burst block (consumed as used)- One-time onboarding & warmup credits: $12,000 (covers pre-warm, shadowing, and runbook creation)

Commercial levers to discuss with procurement:
- 6–12 month stepped commit (start at min 6 GPUs first 30 days, step up by agreed schedule) to lower near-term cashflow- Trial credits (we can authorize up to $30k in platform credits tied to a pilot milestone)- SLA: 99.9% latency SLO on core endpoints with incident playbook included in the first 90 days

If Atlas prefers, we can provide a granular activation calendar (dates + responsible owners) that maps onto your procurement timeline. Grace — do you want me to prepare a 1‑page commercial summary and T&C callouts?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace / Karthik — this is exactly what we needed. Atlas is leaning toward Option B with the stepped commit suggestion (start smaller, scale on defined milestones). Two asks for procurement: 

1) Can Redwood issue a 60-day trial credit line (we'll hit the milestone if our sandbox jobs complete)? Procurement is copied here.
2) Please send a 1-page commercial summary + the activation calendar by COB Tuesday so our legal and procurement teams have something to review ahead of our call.

On the timing: procurement wants the staged cadence in writing (dates and commit breakpoints). If you can map the ramp to specific calendar weeks that would help.

James
